---
title: "Raster data"
description: "Inspect and transform rasters together with vector geometries."
---

<div class="toolbox-kind">Snippet</div>

Raster results are trustworthy only when CRS, resolution, extent and cell alignment are intentional. A matching CRS alone does not guarantee matching cells.

## Packages and import

:::: {.panel-tabset}
### R

```r
library(terra)
library(sf)
library(here)

raw_dir <- here("input", "raw")
processed_dir <- here("input", "processed")
output_dir <- here("output")

rast <- terra::rast(file.path(raw_dir, "land_surface_temperature.tif"))
```

### Python

Use `rasterio` for direct raster I/O and `rioxarray`/`xarray` for labeled multi-band calculations.

```python
from pathlib import Path

import geopandas as gpd
import numpy as np
import rasterio
import rioxarray

raw_dir = Path("input/raw")
processed_dir = Path("input/processed")
output_dir = Path("output")

rast = rioxarray.open_rasterio(
    raw_dir / "land_surface_temperature.tif",
    masked=True,
)
```

## Reproject and align

Choose resampling by data type: typically bilinear/cubic for continuous measurements and nearest-neighbour for categories. When combining rasters, align to a chosen template grid.

:::: {.panel-tabset}
### R

```r
# Reproject continuous data to a CRS.
rast_lv95 <- project(rast, "EPSG:2056", method = "bilinear")

# Align CRS, extent, resolution and origin to an existing template.
rast_aligned <- project(rast, template_rast, method = "bilinear")

# Same CRS but different grid: resample to the template.
rast_resampled <- resample(rast, template_rast, method = "bilinear")

compareGeom(rast_aligned, template_rast, stopOnError = FALSE)
```

### Python

```python
from rasterio.enums import Resampling

# Reproject continuous data to a CRS.
rast_lv95 = rast.rio.reproject(
    "EPSG:2056",
    resampling=Resampling.bilinear,
)

# Match the complete grid of a template raster.
with rioxarray.open_rasterio("input/processed/template_grid.tif", masked=True) as template_rast:
    rast_aligned = rast.rio.reproject_match(
        template_rast,
        resampling=Resampling.bilinear,
    )

assert rast_aligned.rio.crs == template_rast.rio.crs
assert rast_aligned.rio.shape == template_rast.rio.shape
assert rast_aligned.rio.transform() == template_rast.rio.transform()
```

## Crop and mask with vectors

Reproject the vector, not merely its CRS label, to the raster CRS.

:::: {.panel-tabset}
### R

```r
area <- st_read(file.path(raw_dir, "study_area.gpkg"), quiet = TRUE)
area_vect <- area |> st_transform(crs(rast)) |> terra::vect()

# Rectangular crop, followed by an exact geometry mask.
rast_crop <- crop(rast, area_vect)
rast_masked <- mask(rast_crop, area_vect)
```

### Python

```python
area = gpd.read_file(raw_dir / "study_area.gpkg").to_crs(rast.rio.crs)

# Bounding-box crop, followed by an exact geometry mask.
minx, miny, maxx, maxy = area.total_bounds
rast_crop = rast.rio.clip_box(minx=minx, miny=miny, maxx=maxx, maxy=maxy)
rast_masked = rast_crop.rio.clip(area.geometry, area.crs, drop=True)
```

## Mosaic

Adjacent tiles should have compatible CRS, bands and resolution. Decide explicitly how overlaps are resolved.

:::: {.panel-tabset}
### R

```r
tile_paths <- list.files(raw_dir, pattern = "^elevation_tile_.*\\.tif$", full.names = TRUE)
tiles <- sprc(lapply(tile_paths, rast))
rast_mosaic <- mosaic(tiles, fun = "mean")
```

### Python

```python
from contextlib import ExitStack
from rasterio.merge import merge

tile_paths = sorted(raw_dir.glob("elevation_tile_*.tif"))
with ExitStack() as stack:
    sources = [stack.enter_context(rasterio.open(path)) for path in tile_paths]
    mosaic, transform = merge(sources, method="first")
    profile = sources[0].profile.copy()

profile.update(
    height=mosaic.shape[1],
    width=mosaic.shape[2],
    transform=transform,
)
with rasterio.open(processed_dir / "elevation_mosaic.tif", "w", **profile) as dst:
    dst.write(mosaic)
```

## Raster calculations

:::: {.panel-tabset}
### R

```r
# Cell-wise calculation
rast_celsius <- rast - 273.15

# Named-band calculation
ndvi <- (rast[["nir"]] - rast[["red"]]) / (rast[["nir"]] + rast[["red"]])

# Across bands/layers for every cell
rast_mean <- app(rast, mean, na.rm = TRUE)

# Reduce resolution by 4 × 4 cells
rast_coarse <- aggregate(rast, fact = 4, fun = mean, na.rm = TRUE)
```

### Python

```python
# Cell-wise calculation
rast_celsius = rast - 273.15

# Named or indexed bands
red = rast.sel(band=1)
nir = rast.sel(band=2)
ndvi = (nir - red) / (nir + red)

# Across bands for every cell
rast_mean = rast.mean(dim="band", skipna=True)

# Reduce resolution by 4 × 4 cells
rast_coarse = rast.coarsen(x=4, y=4, boundary="trim").mean()
```

## Extract values under points and polygons

:::: {.panel-tabset}
### R

```r
points_vect <- points |> st_transform(crs(rast)) |> vect()
point_values <- extract(rast, points_vect, bind = TRUE)

polygons_vect <- polygons |> st_transform(crs(rast)) |> vect()
polygon_means <- extract(
  rast,
  polygons_vect,
  fun = mean,
  na.rm = TRUE,
  exact = TRUE,
  bind = TRUE
)
```

### Python

```python
points = points.to_crs(rast.rio.crs)
coordinates = [(geometry.x, geometry.y) for geometry in points.geometry]

with rasterio.open(raw_dir / "land_surface_temperature.tif") as src:
    sampled = np.array([values for values in src.sample(coordinates)])

points[[f"band_{i + 1}" for i in range(sampled.shape[1])]] = sampled
```

For polygon summaries, use a tested zonal-statistics implementation and state how partial cells and nodata are handled; those choices can change results.

## Rasterize and vectorize

:::: {.panel-tabset}
### R

```r
# Burn polygon values into an existing template grid.
zones_rast <- rasterize(
  polygons |> st_transform(crs(template_rast)) |> vect(),
  template_rast,
  field = "zone_id",
  touches = TRUE
)

# Convert classified cells to dissolved polygons.
classes_sf <- as.polygons(classified_rast, dissolve = TRUE) |> st_as_sf()
```

### Python

```python
from rasterio.features import rasterize, shapes
from shapely.geometry import shape

polygons = polygons.to_crs(template_crs)
zones = rasterize(
    ((geometry, value) for geometry, value in zip(polygons.geometry, polygons["zone_id"])),
    out_shape=template_shape,
    transform=template_transform,
    fill=0,
    all_touched=True,
    dtype="int32",
)

features = [
    {"value": value, "geometry": shape(geometry)}
    for geometry, value in shapes(classified_array, transform=transform)
    if value != nodata
]
classes_gdf = gpd.GeoDataFrame(features, geometry="geometry", crs=crs)
```

  file.path(output_dir, "land_surface_temperature_study_area.tif"),

  gdal = c("COMPRESS=DEFLATE", "TILED=YES")
)
